## How We Know This {background-color="#f8fafc"}

<div style="font-size:1.05rem; line-height:2.3; max-width:900px;
            margin:1.2rem auto 0; padding:0 1rem; text-align:left;">

1️⃣We used real measurement — NASA tracked Earth's temperature every year since 1990

2️⃣We counted actual Storms — NOAA recorded every hurricane, typhoon, and tornado

3️⃣We looked for patterns - No complex formulas — just comparing temperature to storm counts

4️⃣You be the judge —Every chart on the next slides tells the story

</div>


```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| echo: false

import os, warnings
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from scipy import stats
from IPython.display import Image, display

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# ── Set up absolute paths (works regardless of working directory) ──────────
SCRIPT_DIR = Path.cwd()  # Current directory where Quarto is rendering
DATA_DIR = SCRIPT_DIR / "data"
CHARTS_DIR = SCRIPT_DIR / "charts"
CHARTS_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
print(f"📁 Script directory: {SCRIPT_DIR}")
print(f"📁 Data directory: {DATA_DIR}")

# ── Palette ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C_TEMP    = "#e63946"
C_CYCL    = "#1d3557"
C_INTENSE = "#457b9d"
C_TORN    = "#f4a261"
C_TREND   = "#2a9d8f"
C_BG      = "#F0F4F8"
DECADE_COLORS = {"1990s": "#2a9d8f", "2000s": "#457b9d", "2010s+": "#e63946"}

plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.3,
    "grid.linestyle": "--",
    "figure.facecolor": C_BG,
    "axes.facecolor": "white",
})


# ── Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def load_data():
    try:
        df_t = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "temperature_anomaly.csv")
        df_t.columns = ["year","temp"]
        df_t["temp"] = pd.to_numeric(df_t["temp"], errors="coerce")
        df_t = df_t.dropna()
        print("  ✓ temperature_anomaly.csv loaded")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"  ⚠️ temperature_anomaly.csv not found at {DATA_DIR / 'temperature_anomaly.csv'}")
        print("  → Using embedded fallback data")
        df_t = pd.DataFrame({"year":list(TEMP_DATA.keys()),
                              "temp":list(TEMP_DATA.values())})

    try:
        df_c = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "cyclone_counts.csv")
        df_c.columns = ["year","storms","intense"]
        print("  ✓ cyclone_counts.csv loaded")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"  ⚠️ cyclone_counts.csv not found at {DATA_DIR / 'cyclone_counts.csv'}")
        print("  → Using embedded fallback data")
        df_c = pd.DataFrame({
            "year":    list(CYCLONE_DATA.keys()),
            "storms":  [v[0] for v in CYCLONE_DATA.values()],
            "intense": [v[1] for v in CYCLONE_DATA.values()]
        })

    try:
        df_to = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "tornado_counts.csv")
        df_to = df_to[["year","total_tornadoes"]].rename(
            columns={"total_tornadoes":"tornadoes"})
        print("  ✓ tornado_counts.csv loaded")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"  ⚠️ tornado_counts.csv not found at {DATA_DIR / 'tornado_counts.csv'}")
        print("  → Using embedded fallback data")
        df_to = pd.DataFrame({"year":    list(TORNADO_DATA.keys()),
                               "tornadoes": list(TORNADO_DATA.values())})
    return df_t, df_c, df_to

df_t, df_c, df_to = load_data()
df = (df_t.merge(df_c, on="year").merge(df_to, on="year", how="left"))
df = df[(df.year>=1990)&(df.year<=2024)].sort_values("year").reset_index(drop=True)
df["decade"] = df.year.apply(
    lambda y: "1990s" if y<2000 else ("2000s" if y<2010 else "2010s+"))
df_t2 = df.dropna(subset=["tornadoes"])

# ── Pre-compute all correlations in setup so every cell can use them ───────
r_storms,  p_storms  = stats.pearsonr(df["temp"], df["storms"])
r_intense, p_intense = stats.pearsonr(df["temp"], df["intense"])
r_torn,    p_torn    = stats.pearsonr(df_t2["temp"], df_t2["tornadoes"])

# ── Source annotation helper ───────────────────────────────────────────────
def add_source(ax, text):
    ax.text(0.99, 0.01, text, transform=ax.transAxes,
            fontsize=8, color="#999999", ha="right", va="bottom",
            style="italic")

# ── Save helper ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def save_fig(name):
    path = CHARTS_DIR / f"{name}.png"
    plt.savefig(str(path), dpi=120, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=C_BG)
    plt.close("all")
    return str(path)
```


## ⬆️ Earth Is Getting Warmer Every Year — Faster in Recent Years

```{python}
#| label: chart1
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: 100%

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))

# Color gradient to show acceleration: teal (1990s) → blue (2000s) → red (2010s+)
for i in range(len(df)-1):
    decade = df.iloc[i]["decade"]
    color = DECADE_COLORS[decade]
    ax.plot(df.year.iloc[i:i+2], df.temp.iloc[i:i+2], color=color, lw=3, zorder=3)

ax.fill_between(df.year, 0, df.temp, alpha=0.08, color=C_TEMP)
m, b = np.polyfit(df.year, df.temp, 1)
ax.plot(df.year, m*df.year+b, "--", color="#333", lw=1.5, alpha=0.6,
        label=f"Overall trend: +{m*10:.2f}°C/decade")

ax.axhline(0, color="gray", lw=1, linestyle=":")
ax.set_ylabel("Temperature change (°C)", fontsize=11)
ax.set_xlabel("Year", fontsize=11)
ax.set_title("⬆️ Earth Is Getting Warmer Every Year — Faster in Recent Years", 
             fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")

# Highlight hottest recent years
for yr in [2023, 2024]:
    row = df[df.year==yr]
    if not row.empty:
        ax.scatter(yr, row.temp.values[0], s=120, color="#e63946", zorder=5, edgecolors="white", lw=1)
        ax.annotate(f"{yr}", xy=(yr, row.temp.values[0]),
                    xytext=(yr, row.temp.values[0]+0.11),
                    fontsize=9, fontweight="bold", color="#e63946", ha="center")

ax.annotate("Last 10 years\nhottest ever",
            xy=(2022.3, 1.21), xytext=(2018, 1.21),
            fontsize=9, color="#e63946",
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.4", facecolor="yellow", alpha=0.3))

# Add decade legend
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=DECADE_COLORS["1990s"], alpha=0.8, label="1990s"),
                   Patch(facecolor=DECADE_COLORS["2000s"], alpha=0.8, label="2000s"),
                   Patch(facecolor=DECADE_COLORS["2010s+"], alpha=0.8, label="2010s+")]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc="upper left", fontsize=9, ncol=3, framealpha=0.9)

add_source(ax, "Source: NASA GISTEMP v4")
path = save_fig("chart1_temperature_rise")
display(Image(path))
```

::: {style="font-size:0.88rem; color:#333; text-align:center; margin-top:0.5rem; font-weight:500;"}
📊 **What this shows:** Color changes from teal (1990s) → blue (2000s) → RED (2010s+) to show how warming ACCELERATED. The warming trend is speeding up! Last decade was hottest on record.
:::


## 📊 What The Data Actually Shows

```{python}
#| label: honest_truth
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: 100%

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))

# Plot the actual data points
ax.scatter(df.temp, df.intense, color="#457b9d", s=120, alpha=0.7, zorder=3)

# Add year labels to see the timeline
for _, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.annotate(str(int(row.year)), 
                xy=(row.temp, row.intense),
                xytext=(5, 5), textcoords="offset points",
                fontsize=8, alpha=0.7)

# Add a simple trend line (shows NO relationship)
m, b, r, p, se = stats.linregress(df.temp, df.intense)
x_range = np.linspace(df.temp.min(), df.temp.max(), 100)
ax.plot(x_range, m*x_range + b, '--', color="#888", lw=1.5, alpha=0.5)

# Labels
ax.set_xlabel("Earth's Temperature (°C warmer than 1950s)", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Category 3+ Storms per Year", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_title(" Is There Really a Pattern?", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")

# Honest annotation
ax.text(0.6, 35, f"r = {r:.2f}\n(very weak correlation)", 
        fontsize=11, ha="center", 
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="#fff3cd", alpha=0.9))

# Highlight the truth
ax.text(1.19, 18, "⚠️ No clear pattern!\nHotter years don't always\nmean more storms", 
        fontsize=9, ha="center", color="#e63946",
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="#fdecea", alpha=0.8))

add_source(ax, "Source: NOAA Storm Prediction Center · NASA GISTEMP v4")

path = save_fig("honest_no_pattern")
display(Image(path))
```
::: {style="font-size:0.82rem; color:#555; text-align:center; margin-top:0.5rem;"}
🔍 **What this shows:** Before looking at real data, many people guess: "Hotter Earth = More storms." But when we look at the actual numbers, the story is more complicated. Temperature goes up (top). But storms go up AND down randomly (middle and bottom). This is why scientists use data — to test if our guesses are correct. Sometimes the data surprises us!
:::


## 🌪️ Tornadoes vs. Temperature

```{python}
#| label: chart3_simple
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: 100%

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))

# Plot tornadoes as simple bars
ax1.bar(df_t2.year, df_t2.tornadoes, alpha=0.6, color="#f4a261", width=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel("Year", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
ax1.set_ylabel("Tornadoes Reported in US", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color="#d4821f")
ax1.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="#d4821f")
ax1.set_xlim(1990, 2024)

# Add a BIG shaded area for "The Radar Problem"
ax1.axvspan(1990, 2005, alpha=0.2, color="gray", zorder=0)
ax1.text(1997, 1500, "⚠️ NEW RADAR\n(We got better at finding tornadoes)", 
         fontsize=9, ha="center", fontweight="bold", color="#555",
         bbox=dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="white", alpha=0.8))

# Temperature on right axis
ax2 = ax1.twinx()
ax2.plot(df_t2.year, df_t2.temp, color="#e63946", lw=3, marker="o", markersize=3)
ax2.set_ylabel("Earth's Temperature (°C warmer)", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color="#e63946")
ax2.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="#e63946")

# Simple title
ax1.set_title(" Tornadoes Don't Follow The Same Pattern", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", pad=15)

# Big honest message on the chart
ax1.text(2015, 500, "NO CLEAR PATTERN\nTornado counts go up and down\nbut don't match temperature rise", 
         fontsize=10, ha="center", fontweight="bold", color="#e63946",
         bbox=dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="#fff3cd", alpha=0.95, edgecolor="#e63946", linewidth=2))

add_source(ax1, "NOAA Storm Prediction Center · NASA GISTEMP · 1990-2024")

path = save_fig("chart3_tornadoes_simple")
display(Image(path))
```



::: {style="font-size:0.82rem; color:#555; text-align:center; margin-top:0.5rem;"}
*"In 2005, Doppler radar was fully deployed across America. This improved our ability to detect tornadoes. After 2005, when detection methods became more consistent, tornado counts did not show a clear upward trend with temperature. This teaches us: when looking at data, always consider whether other factors—like changes in technology—might affect what we measure."*
:::

## 📊 What The Data Actually Shows: Temperature vs Storms

```{python}
#| label: chart4_honest
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: 100%

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))

# Scatter plot for intense storms only (clearer)
for dec, grp in df.groupby("decade"):
    ax.scatter(grp.temp, grp.intense, color=DECADE_COLORS[dec],
               s=120, alpha=0.7, edgecolors="white", lw=1.5, 
               label=f"{dec}", zorder=3)

# Add a simple trend line (shows the truth)
m, b, r, p, se = stats.linregress(df.temp, df.intense)
xr = np.linspace(df.temp.min()-0.05, df.temp.max()+0.05, 100)
ax.plot(xr, m*xr+b, "--", color="#666", lw=2, alpha=0.6, 
        label=f"Trend line (r = {r:.2f})")

# Add year labels to see the timeline
for _, row in df.iterrows():
    if row.year in [1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2024]:
        ax.annotate(str(int(row.year)), 
                    xy=(row.temp, row.intense),
                    xytext=(8, 5), textcoords="offset points",
                    fontsize=9, alpha=0.8, fontweight="bold")

# Labels

ax.set_ylabel("Category 3+ Storms per Year", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")

# Legend

add_source(ax, "NOAA Storm Prediction Center · NASA GISTEMP · 1990-2024")

display(Image(path))
```

## 📊 Decade by Decade: Temperature Up, Storms Mixed

```{python}
#| label: chart6_honest
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: 100%

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5))

decade_labels = ["1990s", "2000s", "2010s+"]
dec_temp = [df[df.decade==d].temp.mean() for d in decade_labels]
dec_storms = [df[df.decade==d].intense.mean() for d in decade_labels]
bar_colors = [DECADE_COLORS[d] for d in decade_labels]

# Left: Temperature (clear increase)
b1 = ax1.bar(decade_labels, dec_temp, color=bar_colors, alpha=0.8, width=0.6)
ax1.bar_label(b1, fmt="%.2f°C", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", padding=5)
ax1.set_title(" Temperature", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
ax1.set_ylabel("Temperature Change (°C)", fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylim(0, max(dec_temp) * 1.2)
ax1.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)

# Right: Storms (shows the truth - no clear pattern)
b2 = ax2.bar(decade_labels, dec_storms, color=bar_colors, alpha=0.8, width=0.6)
ax2.bar_label(b2, fmt="%.1f", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", padding=5)
ax2.set_title("Dangerous Storms (Cat 3+)", fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
ax2.set_ylabel("Average Storms per Year", fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylim(0, max(dec_storms) * 1.2)
ax2.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)

fig.suptitle("Temperature Rose Steadily | Storm Pattern Was NOT Clear", 
             fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", y=1.02)

add_source(ax2, "NOAA Storm Prediction Center · NASA GISTEMP · 1990-2024")
path = save_fig("chart6_honest")
display(Image(path))
```

::: {style="font-size:0.82rem; color:#555; text-align:center; margin-top:0.5rem;"}
📈 <strong>Temperature:</strong> Up every decade (CLEAR pattern)<br> 🌀 <strong>Storms:</strong> Up and down (NO clear pattern)<br> 🎓 <strong>Lesson:</strong> Not everything moves together in a simple way!
::: 


## 📊 Looking at the Spread: Year-to-Year Variation Matters

```{python}
#| label: chart7_boxplot
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: 100%

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))

# Create box plot data
storm_by_decade = [df[df.decade==d].intense.values for d in ["1990s", "2000s", "2010s+"]]
positions = [0, 1, 2]

# Box plot
bp = ax.boxplot(storm_by_decade, positions=positions, widths=0.5,
                patch_artist=True, showmeans=True, meanline=True,
                medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color="black"),
                meanprops=dict(linewidth=2, color="blue", linestyle="--"))

# Color the boxes
colors = ["#2a9d8f", "#457b9d", "#e63946"]
box_names = ["1990s", "2000s", "2010s+"]
for patch, color, name in zip(bp['boxes'], colors, box_names):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)

# Add individual points (all years)
for i, decade in enumerate(["1990s", "2000s", "2010s+"]):
    y = df[df.decade==decade].intense.values
    x = np.random.normal(i, 0.05, size=len(y))
    ax.scatter(x, y, alpha=0.6, color="white", edgecolors="#333", s=80, zorder=3)

# Labels
ax.set_xticks(positions)
ax.set_xticklabels(["1990s", "2000s", "2010s+"], fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_ylabel("Category 3+ Storms per Year", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_title("How Storm Numbers Vary Within Each Decade", fontsize=15, fontweight="bold", pad=15)

# Set y-axis limits
ax.set_ylim(10, 45)

# Add annotation for box plot explanation
ax.text(2.5, 42, "BOX = Middle 50% of years\n(25th to 75th percentile)", 
        fontsize=9, ha="center", style="italic", color="#333",
        bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", facecolor="#e8f4f8", alpha=0.9))

ax.text(2.5, 38, "- LINE = Median (middle value)", 
        fontsize=8, ha="center", color="#333")

ax.text(2.5, 35, "--Mean (average)", 
        fontsize=8, ha="center", color="blue")

# Highlight box lengths (variability)
# 1990s box length
ax.annotate("", xy=(0.2, 26), xytext=(0.2, 18),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="<->", color="#2a9d8f", lw=2))
ax.text(-0.3, 22, "Box Height =\nVariability", fontsize=8, ha="center", 
        color="#2a9d8f", fontweight="bold", rotation=90)

# 2000s box length
ax.annotate("", xy=(1.2, 27), xytext=(1.2, 21),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="<->", color="#457b9d", lw=2))

# 2010s box length (LONGEST)
ax.annotate("", xy=(2.2, 35), xytext=(2.2, 22),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="<->", color="#e63946", lw=2.5))
ax.text(2.31, 28, "⬅️ LONGEST BOX\nHighest variability!", fontsize=9, 
        color="#e63946", fontweight="bold")

# Add title for each decade's variability
ax.text(0, 12, "Medium variability", fontsize=9, ha="center", color="#2a9d8f", fontweight="bold")
ax.text(1, 12, "Lowest variability", fontsize=9, ha="center", color="#457b9d", fontweight="bold")
ax.text(2, 12, "HIGHEST variability", fontsize=9, ha="center", 
        color="#e63946", fontweight="bold")

# Add a star/callout for 2010s
ax.annotate("2010s: Most spread out\nSome years: FEW storms\nSome years: MANY storms", 
            xy=(2, 30), xytext=(1.2, 38),
            fontsize=9, ha="left", fontweight="bold", color="#e63946",
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.4", facecolor="#fff3cd", alpha=0.95, edgecolor="#e63946", linewidth=1.5),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#e63946", lw=1.5))

add_source(ax, "NASA GISTEMP · 1990-2024")

plt.tight_layout()
path = save_fig("chart7_boxplot_explained")
display(Image(path))
```
::: {style="font-size:0.82rem; color:#555; text-align:center; margin-top:0.5rem;"}
🔍 <strong>KEY FINDING:</strong> 2010s+ have the LONGEST box— this means the 2010s had the HIGHEST year-to-year variability. Some years (like 2015) had ~40 intense storms, while others (like 2014) had only ~24. The 2000s had the SHORTEST box — storm counts were most consistent during that decade. 
::: 





## What We Learned: {background-color="#f8fafc"}

<div style="font-size:1.05rem; line-height:2.3; max-width:900px;
            margin:1.2rem auto 0; padding:0 1rem; text-align:left; ">
            
Three Things The Data Taught Us

1. Earth Is Warming  — Temperature rose +0.84°C since 1990 — a clear, steady trend

2. Storms Show No Simple Pattern  — Hot years don't always mean more storms — 2024 was hottest but had fewer storms than 2015

3. Real Data Is Messy Science isn't always clean — variability is normal and important to understand


🎓 The most important skill? Looking at data honestly — even when it surprises you.
